title: C Y P two C nine and warfarin

segs.text: Section eleven. C Y P two C nine. C Y P two C nine, short for cytochrome P four fifty two C nine, is a liver enzyme that metabolizes, and so clears, several narrow therapeutic index drugs. These are drugs where a small change in clearance changes the outcome. She said, it does metabolism of a lot of our very narrow therapeutic index drugs, so things like warfarin that we've already talked to some about, and then phenytoin and glipizide. Tolbutamide is the fourth.

Two common variants, star two and star three, make an enzyme with low activity. Compared with the normal enzyme, star one, star two keeps about twenty percent of the activity and star three about five percent. So star three is the more severe loss. The C P I C warfarin guideline reports it another way: S warfarin metabolism drops about thirty to forty percent with star two and eighty to ninety percent with star three. Both say the same thing, less activity.

Why does low activity mean a lower dose? C Y P two C nine clears warfarin. A low activity variant clears it slowly, so the drug builds up. Because the therapeutic index is narrow, the patient moves into the bleeding range unless the starting dose is lowered. These variants lower the dose. They never raise it.

Two studies agree. Warfarin is a mixture of two mirror image forms, R and S warfarin, and S is the more potent. The first study measured clearance. People with two copies of star three cleared S warfarin about ninety percent less than people with two copies of star one. The second study started from the patients who need the lowest dose. The usual starting dose is about five milligrams a day, and these patients need about one point five. She said, at least eighty percent of the people in that dosing category have these low activity variants of two C nine.

How common the variants are differs by population. About thirty percent of Caucasians carry star two or star three, the highest. About one to three percent of African Americans do, but in African ancestry other low activity variants, star five, six, eight and eleven, are together more common. In the East Asians studied, about zero percent carried them, and the C P I C guideline says star two is virtually absent in Asians.

Many drugs also inhibit C Y P two C nine. An inhibitor lowers the enzyme's activity, and a low activity variant lowers it too. The two add up rather than cancel, so a drug the enzyme clears can reach concentrations that are too high.
